title: The Clock of Port Mahon
premise: In 1918, on the British-occupied island of Menorca, apprentice clockmaker Jude Vane is sent to Port Mahon to restore the naval observatory's failing master clock, a job that lets him hide from the war that took his brothers. There he meets Ilse Brenner, a translator for the garrison who recognizes the handwriting in an old letter Jude carries — handwriting belonging to her brother, officially dead at Jutland, whose letters have kept arriving. As the two trace the letters through censored mails and smuggled papers, Jude discovers his late master was part of a network forging identity documents, and the master clock's escapement conceals the workshop's final ledger of names. With the armistice approaching and the network exposed, Jude must choose between shipping the ledger to safety and staying to finish the clock — and Ilse must decide whether the brother she mourns is worth betraying her duty to find. The book ends at the eleventh hour of the eleventh day: the clock strikes true as armistice news reaches the harbor, the ledger reaches its last living name, and Jude and Ilse, no longer invisible, leave Port Mahon together with the truth carried in something small enough to hold.
about_author: Odile Voss is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing Mediterranean port records before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about the small mechanisms — clocks, ledgers, letters — by which ordinary people survive large wars.
